title: An export API with existing customers
summary: Add JSONL export and filtering while preserving every documented CSV behavior.

stages.title: Understand the contract
stages.brief: Add JSONL export and filtering while preserving every documented CSV behavior. Preserve the documented public interface. Use only Python 3.11 standard-library modules.
requirements: Preserve export_orders(orders, format="csv", *, status=None). orders is a one-pass iterable of mappings with order_id, status, and integer amount_cents.
Default CSV must keep header order order_id,status,amount_cents, input row order, standard CSV quoting, LF row endings, and a trailing newline. Empty CSV contains its header.
Add format="jsonl": one compact JSON object per selected row with exactly the three public fields, keys sorted lexically, ensure_ascii=True, and a trailing newline. Empty JSONL is an empty string.
If status is given, include rows with exactly that status in both formats; status=None includes all rows. Unknown statuses simply produce no rows.
Do not mutate inputs or consume the iterable twice. Reject an unsupported format with ValueError before iterating inputs.

stages.title: Implement the change
stages.brief: Make the smallest coherent change that satisfies the disclosed contract.
requirements: Preserve public interfaces and existing valid behavior.

stages.title: Verify the behavior
stages.brief: Run checks and inspect failures before finishing.
requirements: Run public checks and add a targeted boundary or regression check.
Identify behavior that your tests do not establish.

stages.title: Defend your decisions
stages.brief: Explain the submitted code and its remaining limits.
requirements: Use concrete code or test evidence.
Describe one alternative and its trade-off.

rubric.name: Compatibility
rubric.description: Preserve the existing CSV contract while extending behavior.

anchors.strong: Keeps signature, default format, headers, quoting, order, and empty-output behavior.
anchors.developing: Adds the feature but a legacy edge case changes.
anchors.needsWork: Replaces the old output or interface without accounting for existing clients.

anchors.strong: Both formats apply the same exact filter and emit only the documented public fields.
anchors.developing: Implements one format/filter path but misses the other or leaks extra fields.
anchors.needsWork: Ignores requested filters or cannot produce the documented JSONL.

rubric.name: Regression evidence
rubric.description: Test the old contract and new functionality.

anchors.strong: Uses one-pass inputs, escaping, empty outputs, and a format failure check as evidence.
anchors.developing: Tests ordinary JSONL but little legacy behavior.
anchors.needsWork: Assumes a new feature passing means backward compatibility is preserved.

probes.question: Which existing CSV behavior did you verify remained compatible?
How do you ensure status filtering behaves identically for CSV and JSONL?
What would break if a caller supplied a generator rather than a list?

hints: Identify which CSV byte-level details an existing client can observe before changing anything.
Filter a one-pass iterator once, then serialize the selected rows using the requested format.
Use csv.writer for CSV and json.dumps of an explicit three-field mapping for JSONL. Reject unknown formats before consuming the iterator.

drills.title: Extend without changing a default
drills.exercise: Add an optional JSON response to a CSV endpoint. First write a byte-for-byte test for the original default response.

drills.title: Share a filter across serializers
drills.exercise: Given rows with an internal note and two statuses, implement one selection step reused by CSV and JSONL. Prove that the note cannot reach either format.

drills.title: Protect a generator client
drills.exercise: Create a one-use iterator that fails if traversed twice. Verify escaping, empty output, filtering, and early rejection of an unsupported format without consuming it.
